newsitem.title: UK: CRICKET-BALL AND DAVIS SPIN GLOUCESTERSHIRE TOP.
newsitem.headline: CRICKET-BALL AND DAVIS SPIN GLOUCESTERSHIRE TOP.

text.p: Spinners Martyn Ball and Richard Davis bowled Gloucestershire to first place in the English championship on Monday.
They shared nine second innings wickets as Gloucestershire overcame Sussex at Hove by 166 runs.
Although opener Toby Pierce and Neil Taylor shared a second wicket stand of 107, Sussex then folded for 161 in the chase for 328 to win.
Ball took five for 66 and Davis four for 35 as Gloucestershire moved 10 points ahead of second-placed Kent.

Pace bowling prospect Maneer Mirza helped Worcestershire into fourth place by taking the last two Glamorgan wickets in seven balls in a 54-run victory. The defeat at Worcester cost Glamorgan the chance to go top.
Glamorgan, set a target of 374, were dismissed for 319 despite a fifth century of the season by Steve James.
A career-best 145 from Giles White and another century from John Stephenson denied Yorkshire victory at Portsmouth after Hampshire had followed on.
Hampshire began the final day on 173 for three, still needing another 47 to make Yorkshire bat again.
But White, whose previous top score for Hampshire was a modest 73, forced an unlikely draw.
Nottinghamshire wasted a great victory chance against Somerset at Trent Bridge and finished up needing to survive the final over to avoid defeat.
Matthew Dowman cracked his third championship century of the season and Notts appeared to be well on course as they chased a victory target of 320.

But the departures of captain skipper Paul Johnson and Dowman in quick succession sparked a dramatic slide that ended with wicketkeeper Wayne Noon having to play out Mushtaq Ahmed's final over to secure a draw.
The Pakistan leg spinner had been chiefly responsible for the collapse with three for eight in 23 deliveries.
